ruleSummary: The speed limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school while children are outside or crossing the street.
details: Some school zones may have speed limits as low as 15 mph.
exceptions: If the school grounds have no fence and children are outside, never drive faster than 25 mph.

ruleSummary: The speed limit for a blind intersection is 15 mph.
details: An intersection is 'blind' if there are no stop signs at any corner and you cannot see 100 feet in either direction before crossing.

ruleSummary: The speed limit in any alley is 15 mph.
The speed limit is 15 mph within 100 feet of a railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions.
details: You may drive faster if the crossing is controlled by gates, a warning signal, or a flag man.

ruleSummary: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks.
exceptions: Pedestrians must not suddenly leave a curb and walk or run into the path of a vehicle that is so close as to constitute an immediate hazard.

ruleSummary: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or a fire station driveway.
A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking.
exceptions: Transit buses are exempt at designated bus stops.

ruleSummary: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher.
It is illegal for a person under 21 years of age to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.01% or higher.
It is illegal for a person to drive a commercial vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04% or higher.
You must stop from either direction until children are safely across the street and the red lights on the school bus stop flashing.
exceptions: You do not need to stop if the school bus is on the other side of a divided or multilane highway.

ruleSummary: You should signal at least 100 feet before you turn.
details: On a freeway, you should signal for at least 5 seconds before changing lanes.

ruleSummary: You must use your headlights 30 minutes after sunset and leave them on until 30 minutes before sunrise.
You must turn on your low-beam headlights if weather conditions require you to use your windshield wipers.
It is against the law for a minor to use a cell phone or electronic wireless communications device while driving.
exceptions: Exceptions exist for calling emergency services (911) in an emergency situation.

ruleSummary: Use the '3-second rule' to avoid tailgating.
exceptions: Allow a 4-second or more following distance when tailgated, driving on slippery roads, or following motorcyclists/bicyclists on wet or icy roads.

ruleSummary: Use the hand-to-hand steering method (push/pull) for most turning maneuvers.
exceptions: Hand-over-hand steering is recommended when turning at low speeds, parking, or recovering from a skid.

ruleSummary: At a T-intersection without STOP or YIELD signs, vehicles on the through road have the right-of-way.
When two vehicles meet on a steep narrow road where neither can pass, the vehicle facing downhill must yield the right-of-way by backing up.
You may make a U-turn in a residential district if there are no vehicles approaching you within 200 feet.
exceptions: Never make a U-turn in a business district, unless at an intersection or where a sign explicitly permits it.

ruleSummary: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive has the right-of-way.
details: If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

ruleSummary: Traffic travels in a counter-clockwise direction around a roundabout.
details: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Enter heading to the right.

ruleSummary: You must yield to all traffic, including bicyclists and pedestrians, already in the roundabout.
When passing a bicyclist, you must leave at least three feet of space between your vehicle and the bicycle.
exceptions: If 3 feet is not possible, you must slow down and pass only when safe to do so.

ruleSummary: You must yield the right-of-way to a transit bus signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping at a bus stop.
You must yield the right-of-way to any police vehicle, fire engine, or ambulance using a siren and red lights.
details: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
exceptions: Do not stop in an intersection.

ruleSummary: When approaching a stationary emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights, you must move over a lane or slow down.
exceptions: If you cannot move over safely, slow down to a reasonable speed.

ruleSummary: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing.
exceptions: You may cross two solid yellow lines to turn left into a driveway or private road, or make a permitted U-turn.

ruleSummary: A broken yellow line means you may pass if the broken line is next to your driving lane.
Double solid white lines indicate a lane barrier between a regular use and a preferential use lane, such as a carpool/HOV lane. Never cross them.
A center left turn lane is marked by two solid yellow lines on the outside and two broken yellow lines on the inside. You may only drive for 200 feet in this lane.
details: Use it to begin or end a left turn or U-turn.

ruleSummary: You must use a turnout area to let other vehicles pass if you are driving slowly on a two-lane highway or road where passing is unsafe, and there are 5 or more vehicles following you.
You may park in a bicycle lane if your vehicle does not block a bicyclist and there is no 'No Parking' sign posted.
When making a right turn, you must enter the bicycle lane no more than 200 feet before the corner.
You must yield to a blind pedestrian crossing the street with a white cane or a guide dog at all times.
Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A pedestrian you cannot see may be crossing the street.
The maximum speed limit on most California highways is 65 mph.
exceptions: You may drive 70 mph where posted.

ruleSummary: The maximum speed limit on a two-lane undivided highway is 55 mph unless otherwise posted.
The speed limit in business or residential districts is 25 mph unless otherwise posted.
If you see a sign with a picture of an animal, slow down and be prepared to stop. You must obey a person in charge of animals.
California's Basic Speed Law says you may never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
You should scan the road 10-15 seconds ahead of your vehicle so you can see hazards early.
Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds so you know what traffic is doing behind you.
Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before you change lanes, turn, or merge.
If you are tailgating a large truck, you cannot see around it, and the truck driver cannot see you in their rearview mirrors.
When stopping behind a large truck at an intersection, leave extra space in case the truck rolls backward when starting.
Go 5 to 10 mph slower on wet roads.
details: If it is raining hard and you cannot see more than 100 feet ahead, you cannot safely drive faster than 30 mph.

ruleSummary: Cut your speed in half when driving on packed snow.
Slow to a crawl on ice.
In heavy rain at speeds of 50 mph or more, your tires can lose all contact with the road and your vehicle will be riding on water (hydroplaning).
details: If this happens, slow down gradually. Do not apply the brakes.

ruleSummary: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow.
exceptions: High beams will reflect back and cause glare.

ruleSummary: You must dim your high-beam headlights to low beams within 500 feet of a vehicle coming toward you or within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.
A white curb means stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.
A green curb means park for a limited time. Look for a posted sign next to the green zone for time limits.
A yellow curb means stop no longer than the time posted to load or unload passengers or freight.
exceptions: Drivers of noncommercial vehicles are usually required to stay with the vehicle.

ruleSummary: A blue curb means parking is permitted only for a disabled person or driver of a disabled person who displays a placard or special license plate.
When parking downhill on a street with a curb, turn your front wheels into the curb or toward the side of the road.
When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let your vehicle roll back a few inches. The wheel should gently touch the curb.
When parking headed either uphill or downhill when there is no curb, turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.
Your vehicle must be parked parallel to the street and within 18 inches of the curb.
It is illegal to park on a marked or unmarked crosswalk, sidewalk, partially blocking a sidewalk, or in front of a driveway.
It is illegal to park within 7.5 feet of a railroad track.
When entering the freeway, you should enter at or near the speed of traffic.
exceptions: Do not stop before merging into freeway traffic unless it is absolutely necessary.

ruleSummary: Any time you merge with other traffic, you need a gap of at least 4 seconds.
When exiting a freeway, signal your intention for approximately 5 seconds before you reach the exit.
You may pass on the right only when an open highway is clearly marked for two or more lanes of travel in your direction.
exceptions: Never drive off the paved or main-traveled portion of the road or on the shoulder to pass.

ruleSummary: It is illegal to drink any amount of alcohol, or smoke or ingest any cannabis product while driving or riding as a passenger in a motor vehicle.
exceptions: Containers of alcohol must be full, sealed, and unopened. Otherwise they must be kept in the trunk.

ruleSummary: A DUI conviction remains on your driving record for 10 years.
By driving in California, you consent to have your breath, blood, or urine tested if you are arrested for driving under the influence (Implied Consent Law).
It is illegal to drive after taking any medication that impairs your ability to drive safely.
details: This includes prescription and over-the-counter medications.

ruleSummary: Drivers 18 and older may use a cell phone only if it is hands-free, such as Bluetooth or a mounted device.
details: The device must be mounted on the windshield, dashboard, or center console, and only require a single swipe or tap to use.

ruleSummary: It is illegal to wear a headset or earplugs in both ears while driving.
exceptions: Persons operating authorized emergency vehicles or special construction equipment.

ruleSummary: You and all passengers must wear a seat belt or you may be cited.
details: If your passenger is under 16 years old and not wearing a seat belt, you will be cited.

ruleSummary: Children under 8 years old, or who are less than 4 feet 9 inches tall, must be properly secured in a federally-approved child passenger restraint system in the rear seat.
Children under 2 years old must be secured in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system unless the child weighs 40 pounds or more or is 40 or more inches tall.
It is illegal to leave a child 6 years of age or younger unattended in a motor vehicle.
exceptions: The child may be left under the supervision of a person 12 years of age or older.

ruleSummary: If you are involved in a collision resulting in an injury, death, or property damage over $1,000, you must report it to the DMV within 10 days.
If you hit a parked vehicle or other property, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address securely attached to the vehicle or property.
details: You must also report the collision to the city police or CHP.

ruleSummary: You must carry written evidence of financial responsibility (insurance) at all times and present it when pulled over by law enforcement or after a collision.
Minimum insurance in California is $15,000 for single injury/death, $30,000 for multiple injury/death, and $5,000 for property damage.
It is illegal to smoke in a motor vehicle when a minor (under 18 years old) is present.
details: You can be fined up to $100.

ruleSummary: It is a criminal offense to dump or abandon an animal on a highway.
details: Punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, 6 months in jail, or both.

ruleSummary: You may not carry anything in or on a passenger vehicle which extends beyond the fenders on the left side or more than 6 inches beyond the fenders on the right side.
Cargo extending more than 4 feet from the back rear bumper of the vehicle must display a 12-inch red or fluorescent orange square flag or two red lights at night.
Littering on the roadside carries a fine of $1,000 and you may be forced to pick up what you threw away.
Only use your horn to avoid collisions, to alert another driver of a hazard, or on narrow mountain roads where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead.
exceptions: Do not use your horn to express anger or to encourage a driver to go faster.

ruleSummary: With a provisional permit, you must be accompanied by a licensed parent, guardian, or other licensed driver 25 years of age or older at all times.
details: They must sit close enough to take control of the vehicle if necessary.

ruleSummary: A provisional instruction permit does not allow you to drive alone at any time, not even to a DMV office to take a driving test.
During the first 12 months after receiving a provisional license, you cannot transport passengers under 20 years old.
exceptions: Unless accompanied by a licensed parent, guardian, or licensed driver 25 years or older.

ruleSummary: During the first 12 months, you cannot drive between 11 PM and 5 AM.
exceptions: Exceptions exist for medical necessity, school activities, or employment, provided you carry a signed note.

ruleSummary: Allow a four-second following distance for motorcycles. When they brake, you may not see their brake lights if they only downshift.
Motorcyclists are permitted to lane split in California.
details: Do not intentionally block or impede a motorcyclist in a way that could cause harm.

ruleSummary: Large trucks have much larger blind spots (No Zones) than passenger vehicles. If you cannot see the truck driver in their side mirror, they cannot see you.
Large trucks take longer to stop and need more room to turn. They often swing wide to the left to make a right turn.
Never turn in front of an approaching light rail vehicle. They cannot steer off the tracks to avoid a collision.
A flashing red traffic signal light means 'STOP.' After stopping, you may proceed when it is safe.
A solid yellow traffic signal light means 'CAUTION.' The red traffic signal light is about to appear. Stop if you can do so safely.
A flashing yellow traffic signal light warns you to 'PROCEED WITH CAUTION.' Slow down and be alert before entering the intersection.
A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn, but your turn is not protected from other traffic. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
If a traffic signal light is not working (blackout), you must treat the intersection as if it is controlled by STOP signs in all directions.
